sections.name: Alligator
sections.card:
Summary: A large reptile of Bayou Nwa in Lemoyne, also found in Bluewater Marsh and parts of Scarlett Meadows around the Kamassa River. It comes in a regular and a small size, and it clamps its jaws on your torso and swings you about, killing you almost instantly.
Weak points: A rifle pierces its tough armoured body plates, and a single rifle shot to the head kills it. A tomahawk thrown at its head kills it instantly, and a bow shot with improved or poisoned arrows straight into the head is a good alternative.
Looks like: Green, scaly skin, a long tail, a large gaping mouth and eyes that stick out from either side of the head.
Tips: A scoped rifle lets you kill one from farther away without getting close. Alligators cannot be skinned in water, so it is best to find and kill one lying on the shore; most of them lie still near the shores of Bayou Nwa and only attack or fight back if you come too close. Small alligators flee when you approach, and your horse gets spooked and throws you off if you ride toward a gator.

sections.name: Boar
sections.card:
Summary: A wild omnivore found in New Hanover, Lemoyne and West Elizabeth, with the greatest concentration throughout Lemoyne. It drops a boar pelt, tender pork loin, animal fat and a boar tusk.
Weak points: A rifle, or a bow with poison arrows, is the easiest way to take down an animal of its size.
Tips: You can get a perfect pelt with a rifle, or with a bow using poison or regular arrows. Although it counts as a large animal, a boar can only be skinned like the massive animals such as elk and bison, so it cannot be picked up and stored on your horse.

sections.name: Snake
sections.card:
Summary: Most snakes are venomous and bite if provoked, and they are found in virtually all locations, in higher numbers along the eastern regions, especially Bluewater Marsh and Bayou Nwa. They drop stringy meat, snake skin and a snake carcass.
Weak points: The page names none; snakes try to flee from you, and for a perfect snake skin you have to use a bow with small game arrows.
Tips: A Health Cure removes the venom from you, and horses are always spooked by snakes. Any perfect snake skin, not just a rattlesnake's, can be used to craft the Rattlesnake Vaquero Saddle from the Trapper, which the page calls arguably the best saddle in the game for all-around balance.

sections.name: Lemoyne Raiders
sections.card:
Summary: A gang that terrorizes Scarlett Meadows most of all, and the areas around Rhodes and Saint Denis, often with crimes like murder and robbery. They are regularly successful because of their manpower and ammunition.
Weak points: The page names none; it says their strength is manpower and ammunition.
Looks like: Every member wears a grey Confederate-military style uniform with a yellow neckerchief.
Tips: A gang of 8 to 12 mounted Raiders can storm you without warning under the rail bridge near Hill Haven Ranch, and the page says deaths in that ambush are notoriously common. Another ambush near Catfish Jacksons uses a wagon-mounted Gatling gun and then reinforcements, and with no cover it is a hard fight. Two unique hats, the Military Officer's Hat and the Military Forage Cap, can be kept from some enemies in random Raider camps.

sections.name: Murfree Brood
sections.card:
Summary: A cruel, territorial gang that the page says is intent on controlling the local area and keeping people in terror. They do not camp in the wilderness: you usually meet them while they are looting a travellers' camp.
Weak points: The page names none; it says they are unusually durable for human enemies, and have survived point-blank shotgun blasts and in some cases even headshots with lesser firearms.
Looks like: They rarely wear shirts.
Tips: They frequently use Volcanic Pistols and double-barreled shotguns, which makes close combat with them very deadly. Murfrees do not carry valuables, so looting them mostly gives cigarettes, tonics and herbs, although Murfrees in scripted ambushes always carry money. Their throwing knives can be looted from them too.

sections.name: Dynamite
sections.card:
Summary: A thrown explosive with very high power but low range and low accuracy, of which you can carry up to 8. It cannot be customized.
Uses: It can clear out groups of enemies, or blow up mines, trains and safes. Light it and throw it at your target, or put it down, light it and run to a safe distance. It can also blow fish out of the water, but the fish will be of poor quality and you lose a small amount of Honor.
Tips: You cannot buy it from gunsmiths, though some less-than-reputable sellers may stock it; every fence sells it after the mission "Who the Hell is Leviticus Cornwall?", and some missions hand it out. Shooting dynamite makes it explode, including the crates of dynamite found around the map. A Volatile Dynamite pamphlet gives a version with a wider explosion radius, more damage and the ability to ignite a fire, crafted from regular dynamite, animal fat and any type of high velocity cartridge; dynamite can also be used to craft dynamite arrows that explode on impact.

sections.name: Fire bottle
sections.card:
Summary: A glass bottle of flammable spirits with a cloth fuse that causes a large fireball on impact. It has high power, low range and low accuracy, and it cannot be customized.
Uses: It is useful for setting fire to stagecoaches or forcing people and animals to retreat.
Tips: You can craft one by combining any type of alcoholic spirit with animal fat, or buy one from some less-than-reputable sellers. Every fence sells it after the mission "The Fine Joys of Tobacco", and you can get one earlier by looting enemies. Upgrading the ammo cart to max level provides two fire bottles. The Volatile Fire Bottle does more damage and has a better impact radius, and is crafted from 1 animal fat and 1 moonshine once you have its pamphlet.

sections.name: Tomahawk
sections.card:
Summary: A lightweight thrown axe with moderate power, low range and low accuracy, which can also be used as a close-range melee weapon. It cannot be customized.
Uses: It is ideal for quick thrown attacks, and you can save a trip by picking it up again after throwing. Thrown at an alligator's head, it kills the animal instantly.
Tips: You can buy one from some less-than-reputable sellers, and after the mission "The First Shall Be Last" it is available from all fences and the Trapper. Earlier, you can pick one up at Six Point Cabin before the mission "Paying a Social Call" while the hideout is not occupied yet, or find one on broken abandoned stagecoaches around Southern Cumberland Forest.

sections.name: Throwing knife
sections.card:
Summary: A small, balanced knife with moderate power, moderate accuracy and low range, thrown at enemies or used in melee. It cannot be customized.
Uses: It can silently take down enemies at range, and you can save a trip by picking it up again after throwing. Unlike the hunting knife, a throwing knife and its variants can trigger an instant melee takedown if you equip it and aim at an aggressive enemy at close range.
Tips: A poisoned throwing knife, crafted at a campfire from a throwing knife and Oleander Sage, guarantees certain death for an NPC once any attack with it starts, and it makes legendary animals and dangerous wild animals such as grizzly bears, cougars and panthers run away after one attack; it turns back into a regular knife once you recover it. The improved throwing knife, crafted at a campfire from a throwing knife and rare bird feathers, may guarantee an instant kill where a regular one can be survived. You get your first one in the mission "Paying a Social Call", and a fence or the Trapper sells them after it.

sections.name: Sawed-off shotgun
sections.card:
Summary: A two-shot shotgun with high power but low range and low accuracy, made for close quarters on foot or on horseback. It can be fired with one hand or dual wielded, and unlike other shotguns it occupies a holster/handgun slot.
Uses: Dual wielding it with a second sawed-off shotgun is highly effective for quickly eliminating anything in your way, man or beast. It takes regular buckshot, incendiary buckshot, slug and explosive slug.
Tips: You are given one in the mission "Enter, Pursued by a Memory", and you can buy a second from any gunsmith for $85.

sections.name: Cattleman Revolver
sections.card:
Summary: The revolver you have from the start of the game, a classic all-around sidearm with a good balance of damage, accuracy and fire rate. It holds six rounds and can be dual-wielded and used on horseback.
Uses: It suits close to medium range, and fires fast from the hip. Rifling improves its range, and a longer barrel and improved iron sights improve its accuracy. It can take 3 to 4 shots to kill an NPC hit in the torso, but a single shot to the head, neck or upper chest is enough.
Tips: It takes regular, high velocity, split point, express and explosive revolver ammo. You can buy a second one from any gunsmith or pick one up from slain NPCs. Once your Honor rank is +4 or higher, the Hero's Pearl Grip becomes purchasable at any gunsmith for this weapon only.

sections.name: Bolt Action Rifle
sections.card:
Summary: A strong, versatile rifle with five rounds, high power, high range and very high accuracy, but a low rate of fire. It costs $180.
Uses: It is an ideal choice for long-range combat with multiple targets, and with a scope attached it becomes a good substitute for the Carcano Rifle.
Tips: It takes regular, high velocity, split point, express and explosive rifle ammo. It is provided in the Chapter 3 mission "Preaching Forgiveness as He Went" and is then available from all gunsmiths; it can also sometimes be found on lawmen during public executions in Valentine and Saint Denis.

sections.name: Carcano Rifle
sections.card:
Summary: A long, scoped bolt-action sniper rifle with six rounds, high power, very high range and very high accuracy, a low rate of fire and a high reload speed. It costs $190.
Uses: Its quick reload speed makes it ideal for facing several enemies in long-distance combat.
Tips: It takes regular, high velocity, split point, express and explosive rifle ammo. It is free during two story missions, the first being "The Delights of Van Horn", and is then available from all gunsmiths. You must look down its scope whatever camera mode you use.

sections.name: Pump-Action Shotgun
sections.card:
Summary: The Lancaster pump-action shotgun, with five rounds, moderate power, low range and low accuracy, and a large ammo capacity and quick reload. It costs $148.
Uses: The page says it holds true when you are confronted by a wild beast or a man in close combat. It takes regular buckshot, incendiary buckshot, slug and explosive slug.
Tips: It is available from all gunsmiths after the mission "Pouring Forth Oil IV", and you can also take it for free at Chez Porter from a weapon case at the top of the ladder in the master bedroom. Your ammo maximum is 60, or 90 with the upgraded bandolier.
